header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:defix:edh:pannonia-inferior-lat:lat, from the Epigraphic Database Heidelberg (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. notes.72436.1: Two tablets. 72436: 'respectes' is taken as the name Respectus (genitive with 'tongue'); 'Ammionis' may instead go with the line before ('the fellow slaves of Ammio'); 'Surus' may be a name or 'the Syrian'; 'Annia' may be Annia or a shortened Annianus; L[...]CO and ECCIGNISN are unread; 'ob' may begin a verb such as obligo, 'I bind'. 82820: the edition's corrections of the tablet's letters (<Dis=ITO> etc.) are translated as corrected. Aeracura is a consort of Dis Pater. 'an(t)epistula' seems to mean a counter-letter, perhaps a counter-spell. 'Muta et Tacita' may instead mean '[may it be] mute and silent', of that letter. Tricerberus is three-headed Cerberus, though the commands are plural; 'illu[...]' may be illuc, 'there'. Line 6: 'loqui' taken with Gaius and Iulia (the clause otherwise lacks a verb); it could instead close the previous line's curse on Asellio, 'to act [or] to speak'.

nodes.text: Iulia Nissa and Gaius Mutilius: may [they] not be able to act
against Oceanus, against Amoenus; may Gaius not be able against Felicio
to act; may the tongue of Respectus (?) not be able [to act] against the fellow slaves;
may Ammio's (?) tongue not be able [...]
to act; may the tongue of Eunicus Surus not be able [to act] against Oceanus;
may the tongue and name of Asellio not be able to act against Oceanus
may neither Gaius nor Iulia be able to speak against Annia;
may the tongue of Annianus not be able [...]
-nus to act; and may the tongue and name of Decibalus not be
able to act against Oceanus. In the same way as I write this with a
reversed stylus, so [may] their tongues [be] reversed, so that they may not be able
to act against these, L[...]CO, [whom] I have set down above; may neither Gaius nor Iul[ia]
Nissa and Eunicus Surus, against Oceanus, [their] ton[gu]es
ob [...]AE[...] tongu[e ...]ECCIGNISN[...]
against Amoenus [...]
Dis Pater, Aeracura, M[er]cury
of Cyllene, these name[s]
I declare to yo[u], that you hand [them] over to the dire
hounds — divine Manes — of Tartarus:
Marcus, Marcia, Chariton,
Secundus; whoev[er]
rises up as an adversary,
who would br[ing] you a counter-letter —
Muta and Tacita!
As the Manes are mute and
silent, so may those who bring you a
counter-letter be mu[te]
and silent. The adversaries
of Bellicus — receive [them], Tricer[be]rus,
and hold [them] illu[...]
